    Kernels of surjections in a stable family are polynomially covered #

    Let H be a space of linear maps M → N with dim N + 1 = dim M, and let E be a space of endomorphisms of N containing the identity with E H ⊆ H. The kernel vectors of the surjective maps in H are covered by finitely many images of polynomial maps from k^(dim H - dim E + 1) (kernel_polyCovered).

    The proof slices the free action of the invertible elements of E by affine coordinate charts of H. For a surjective h, the map g ↦ g h embeds E into H; some coordinate projection onto dim E coordinates is bijective on its image. Prescribing those coordinates from a finite grid determines g, and a grid point with det g ≠ 0 exists because the determinant is a nonzero polynomial of bounded degree. The kernel line of the resulting surjection is read off by kernelVec.
